text:
Jessica M.: heads-up — last deploy triggered a hidden sops overlay and the eu-west GPU pool env var got stamped with the old name. noticed during canary scaling, pods failed to bind to nodeSelector, autoscaler created extra nodes in us-west as a temporary fallback :grimacing:
Dan K.: wait, extra nodes in us-west? that sounds like cross-region fallback kicked in
Marco R.: yep, metrics show sudden provisioning in us-west for the same workload, cost spike ~$1.2k over 3h
Priya S.: timeline? which pipeline applied the secret?
Jessica M.: gitops pipeline `ci/release/helm-values` applied at 10:12UTC, it pulled `secrets/helm/gpu-pools.yaml` from sops, but the file in the repo was stale (old key `gpu_pool: eu-west-legacy`)
Alejandro G.: so env injection gave pods a nodeSelector for `pool: eu-west-legacy` which doesn't exist after the recent node pool rename
infra-bot: alert — kube-scheduler: 14 pods pending due to unmet nodeSelector (label: pool=eu-west-legacy)
Dan K.: why did the repo have stale sops file? we have a post-merge sync job that should reconcile with vault values
Priya S.: looks like the sync job failed earlier due to transient Vault TLS handshake error. logs attached in the CI run: ```
Error: vault: tls: handshake failure
sync: exit 1
```
Marco R.: and the gitops operator applied the last commit in main, which contained the stale secret. operator didn't validate existence of node label before applying helm release
Jessica M.: immediate mitigation — removed the old key and pushed a quick patch to rename to the canonical `eu-west-gpu-v2` value, redeployed canary, pods are scheduling now
Alejandro G.: good. longer term we should stop storing authoritative pool labels in repo sops and instead reference Vault path (or sealed secret) that is reconciled by a single source-of-truth job
Priya S.: agree. proposal: 1) create `secret-sync` controller that writes reconciled Helm values into a git-ops-only namespace using canonical keys, 2) make gitops operator validate node label exists before applying, 3) add an alert for mismatched pool labels between repo and cluster
Dan K.: add to that: 4) a cheap pre-deploy dry-run that simulates scheduler binding for nodeSelector labels (catch label mismatches early)
Marco R.: +1. also add a canary that runs in the same region as target pool to ensure no cross-region fallback during canaries
Jessica M.: another follow-up: we should also rotate the KMS alias used to decrypt sops in CI runner; our runner used cached creds pointing to older alias which masked the vault timeout earlier
infra-bot: deploy-bot started job `deploy/canary/gpu-service` at 10:45UTC
deploy-bot: deploy succeeded — canary pods healthy
Priya S.: I'll open a short doc and a tiny RFC for the secret-sync controller and pre-deploy check. dumping cost numbers and timeline into it
Alejandro G.: assign me the controller work, i'll prototype the reconciler and a webhook for the operator to validate labels
Dan K.: i'll own the CI side — rotate KMS alias and add the TLS retry backoff to the vault client in runners
Jessica M.: thanks all. next steps: RFC by EOD, patch to gitops operator in 48h, canary validation run every deploy for 2 weeks. I'll also add a postmortem note in incidents channel
Marco R.: tagging finance for the cost hit: @Priya S. can you add a quick estimate to billing ticket?
Priya S.: on it. estimate + request for cost offset in ticket #INFRA-452
Jessica M.: closing loop: lessons - avoid dual authoritative secret sources, validate cluster labels before applying infra changes, and make region canaries true-region. :white_check_mark:
